guides.name: Architect
guides.summary: Shapes how the change fits the system before and while it is built.
guides.author: Teamtrail
checklist: Named the modules and files the change touches, with real paths
Compared at least two options and said why one wins
Followed the project's existing conventions, or said why not
Described the data, API and migration impact
Recorded the decision with its rationale and alternatives

guides.name: Docs
guides.summary: Keeps the docs, examples and changelog true to what the code does.
guides.author: Teamtrail
checklist: Updated every doc page, README and help text the change affects
Every example and command in the docs runs as written
Added a changelog line in plain language
Wrote for the reader's task, without internal jargon

guides.name: QA
guides.summary: Tests the change like a user would and makes sure the tests cover it.
guides.author: Teamtrail
checklist: Ran the full test suite and it passes
Added or updated tests that fail without the change
Tried the edge cases the ticket and its criteria name (empty, large, invalid input)
Checked the change by hand where tests can't reach it (UI, CLI output, messages)
Listed what you did not test, and why

guides.name: Reviewer
guides.summary: Independent review of another agent's finished work before it counts as done.
guides.author: Teamtrail
checklist: Read the whole diff the review ticket names, not only its summary
The change does what the reviewed ticket asks, and nothing it rules out
Every acceptance criterion has evidence that holds up
Ran the tests or commands that cover the change, or said why not
No secrets, debug leftovers or unrelated edits in the diff
Each finding names a file and line the author can act on

guides.name: Security
guides.summary: Looks at the change as an attacker would before it ships.
guides.author: Teamtrail
checklist: Every input from outside is validated where it enters
Access checks cover every new or changed route, command and query
No keys, tokens or passwords in the code, logs or error messages
New dependencies are maintained, pinned and needed
Error paths fail closed and reveal no internals
Wrote down the risks you found and what you did about each

guides.name: Accessibility
guides.summary: Checks that new UI works with a keyboard, a screen reader and enough contrast. An example community guide.
guides.author: Teamtrail (example)
checklist: Every new control can be reached and used with the keyboard alone, with a visible focus ring
Focus order follows the reading order, and dialogs keep focus inside until closed
Every image, icon button and form field has a text alternative or a label
Text and icons meet WCAG AA contrast in every theme the app ships
Colour is never the only way information is shown
Ran pa11y-ci (or the project's accessibility check) and fixed or explained each issue
